screenshots.caption: The login screen before any credentials are entered: email, password and the single Log in action.
screenshots.note: The entry point for every journey in this pack.

screenshots.caption: Login with a wrong password: the generic "Invalid email or password." alert. The wording is identical for an unknown email, so it does not reveal whether an account exists.
screenshots.note: TEST-02 and TEST-03 assert the same response against the API; TEST-04 covers the 400 field-validation shape.

screenshots.flow: Menu browsing, available and sold out
screenshots.caption: Customer menu at desktop width: THB prices, a "1 left" stock hint on Mango Sticky Rice, "Sold out" badges on Chicken Sandwich and Pad Thai, and the empty cart panel.
screenshots.note: Availability is computed by the shared isOrderable rule (TEST-10, TEST-11).

screenshots.caption: The same catalogue at 430 px width: the sold-out badges, the low-stock hint, the disabled Add buttons and the anonymous "Log in to order" action all stay visible.
screenshots.note: Responsive evidence; the desktop view is E-03.

screenshots.flow: Cart filled before placing an order
screenshots.caption: Cart with Basil Pork Rice x2 and Thai Iced Tea x1, per-line totals, estimated total THB 150.00 and an empty pickup note.
screenshots.note: The cart total is an estimate; the authoritative total is recalculated by the server (TEST-15).

screenshots.flow: Unavailable item rejected without losing the cart
screenshots.caption: The stale-cart case: an inline alert reads "Mango Sticky Rice is sold out." while both cart lines and the total stay on screen and no navigation occurs.
screenshots.note: The cart survives the 409; TEST-30 asserts the same behaviour in a component test.

screenshots.flow: Order confirmation and customer order detail (PENDING)
screenshots.caption: Immediately after a successful POST: order CB-000003 with Pending and Unpaid badges, both lines with unit prices and totals, THB 150.00, the pickup note, and the first history entry "Order placed" by CUSTOMER with a timestamp.
screenshots.note: This screen is also the confirmation step: the SPA navigates straight to the detail after a 201.

screenshots.caption: My orders: CB-000003 and CB-000002 Pending, CB-000001 Accepted, newest first, each with its placed time and total.
screenshots.note: TEST-28 asserts that only the caller's orders are returned, newest first.

screenshots.caption: Operator "Incoming orders" with the Pending filter active: two PENDING orders with distinct placed times, CB-000001 above CB-000002, each with an Accept button.
screenshots.note: TEST-32 asserts the oldest-first ordering; this capture shows two orders with different timestamps.

screenshots.caption: The acceptance action itself: row CB-000001 while still PENDING, with its green Accept button before the click.
screenshots.note: Captured from the row element so the button and the status it acts on are unambiguous.

screenshots.caption: After accepting, on the unfiltered All view: CB-000001 is ACCEPTED with no action button, while CB-000002 remains PENDING with its Accept button.
screenshots.note: The All filter avoids showing an ACCEPTED row under the PENDING filter after the in-place row update.

screenshots.caption: The same order as the customer sees it: CB-000001 Accepted, with a two-row history, "Order placed" by CUSTOMER then "Pending to Accepted" by OPERATOR, each with a timestamp.
screenshots.note: TEST-41 drives this journey end to end.

screenshots.flow: Customer blocked from an operator screen
screenshots.caption: A customer opening the operator orders route sees the in-place "403 Forbidden: You have no access to this page." alert instead of the order table.
screenshots.note: TEST-42 asserts the in-place alert; TEST-37 and TEST-38 assert the API returns 403 with no order data.

screenshots.flow: Logout returns to the login form
screenshots.caption: After logout the session cookie is cleared and the browser is back at the empty login form.
screenshots.note: The screenshot is byte-identical to E-01 by design: both are the same empty login form, captured with animations disabled. TEST-06 supplies the proof that the session is really gone - it asserts the old cookie is rejected with 401 and that the browser URL is /login.
